newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fortis 9 month profit up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fortis 9 month profit up 18 pct.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis on Thursday announced an 18 percent rise in net profits over the first nine months of 1996 to 554 million ECUS ($696.7 million) and targeted a growth of 12 to 15 percent for the year.
The group's full-year forecast is an upgrading of its estimate earlier this year when it said profits were likely to increase by at least 10 percent in 1996.
"In view of the fine results, Fortis is raising its forecast," it said in a statement.
Analysts were upbeat on the results and forecast.

"The general impression is positive. Good figures," said analyst Jacob Bosscha of Bank Labouchere, adding he was raising his full-year forecast. "My full-year forecast might go up a few cents (per share) but it won't be a drastic revision," he said.
Dutch Fortis Amev, one of the two parent companies of Fortis, posted a net profit of 605 million guilders ($351.7 million) versus 519 million guilders in the same period of 1995.
Dutch Amev merged with Belgian AG in 1989.
Fortis AG's profit rose by 21 percent during the first nine months of 1996 to 10.052 billion Belgian francs.
Fortis upgraded the profit forecast for both parent companies for the whole of 1996, saying it was expecting an increase in net profits per share of at least 10 percent for the two.
"Life business (in the Netherlands) achieved a handsome increase thanks to higher investment and mortality results and better cost control," Fortis said.

"The growth of corporate credit operations required a higher addition to the provision for general banking risks," Fortis said. "Furthermore, a provision has been made for the restructuring of the foreign exchange activities," it added.
As result of this the operating banking result in the Netherlands was 8 percent lower than the same period last year at 67 million ECU.
In Belgium the operating result for banking showed an increase of 25 percent to 332 million ECUS compared to the same period of 1995.
"Banking was slightly better than expected," said analyst Dick Erdman of Gilissen Bankiers.
Analyst Ton Gietman of Van Meer James Capel said Fortis had said at the interims they expected banking to show clearly lower profits in the second half because last year was very good.
"But this did not happen in the third quarter," Gietman said.
Shares in Fortis Amev, slightly up before the nine months figures were released, rose further in early afternoon to 56.80 guilders, up 1.70 guilders.
One analyst said he had the shares at a strong buy, saying in the short-term the shares could rise to 65 guilders.
Shares in Fortis AG gained 50 Belgian francs to 4890, after lingering at flat levels before the figures were announced.
-- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000 ($ = 0.795 European Currency Unit ECUs) ($ = 1.720 Dutch Guilders)
